bull_case: 유리한 사업·자본배분 가정이 유지되면 기준 점수보다 높은 결과가 가능하다.
bear_case: 성장·마진·자본배분이 정상화되고 핵심 불확실성이 불리하게 전개되면 기준 점수보다 낮아질 수 있다.
thesis: Berkshire has exceptional duration but not outlier-scale growth. The long-term case is steady compounding plus disciplined capital allocation, not a five-year doubling of the operating base.

evidence.claim: H1 2026 operating earnings rose to $24.329B from $20.801B.
Berkshire operates across multiple long-duration industries.
Greg Abel became CEO Jan.1 2026 after a planned succession.
P/B 1.47 was near the 5-year average 1.49 at the cutoff.

counterevidence: Scale creates a high denominator for future growth.
T-bill accumulation shows high-return opportunities do not always match cash generation.
Several key subsidiaries are mature and capital intensive.
unknowns: Five-year normalized owner-earnings CAGR after 2026 acquisitions.
falsifiers: Five-year owner earnings fail to grow at least mid-single digits.
Capital deployment remains structurally below cash generation.

subscores.rationale: Base owner-earnings path grows only about 1.25x over five years, below the 1.5x rubric threshold; $1T scale limits plausible doubling.
Diversified insurance/infrastructure/industrial franchises and acquisition capacity support 5–10 year economic growth.
Decentralization and cross-industry capital reallocation show durable adaptive culture, though CEO succession is new.
price/Base≈0.80 is a concrete expectation gap, but P/B 1.47 is near the five-year average, so mispricing is not extreme.
